reason: I’ll add the receiving branches first because their picture shows where they fit on the cell bodies.
expectation: I expect the branches to attach to the nerve-cell bodies, making structures that can receive messages.

alternatives.reason: The channels also fit a goal and appear to let charged particles cross the fibre membrane, but I’ll build the receiving side first.

effect: The receiving branches are in place, but the long extensions still need to be added.
reaction: It makes sense that the branches share the cell's membrane.
reason: I'll fit the channels into the long fibres to work on the other goal. The picture shows that ions can pass through their open gates.
expectation: I expect the channels to be placed in the fibre membranes, allowing charged particles to cross when the gates open.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the fibres to the cells first, but I'll prepare their channels first.

effect: The channels are fitted, and the picture shows how an electrical change moves along the fibre without one particle travelling the whole way. Now the parts need joining.
reaction: The idea of neighbouring channels opening in turn makes the message easier to picture; the pump's details are less clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it joins the receiving regions to the prepared extensions.
expectation: I expect complete nerve cells with receiving branches and long extensions containing channels.

effect: The joined nerve cells show how receiving branches and channel-filled extensions fit together, and that chemical messengers cross a gap to the next cell.
reaction: The separate membranes at the contact were a useful detail; I hadn't expected the chemical messenger step.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the channels was most worthwhile: the sequence of neighbouring channels opening made it easier to picture an electrical change moving along a fibre.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the receiving branches was straightforward but less interesting; it mostly confirmed where they fit.

surprise.text: I was surprised that no single charged particle has to travel the whole length for the electrical change to pass along.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt purposeless, though I followed the offered pairing for the channels and didn't fully understand how the existing pump works.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing how a nerve cell passes a message to another cell makes me curious about what happens next.
